clue.text: Disney's film business doubled

indicators.note: doubled tells you to write the abbreviation twice, side by side

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a business
the same abbreviation again, as the doubling asks

explanation.surface: A report on how Disney's movie trade has grown twice as big.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco is the 2017 Pixar animated feature released by Disney, set during the Mexican Day of the Dead.

clue.text: In religious residence, sex is a pressing matter

indicators.note: In places one word inside the other, the residence holding the sex

parts.note: a priory is a house of monks or nuns
IT is a old slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A racy suggestion that in a monastery, sex is urgently on everyone's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex is old slang, as in the 'It girl' of the 1920s; the residence opens just before its last letter to take it.
explanation.definitionFit: A priority is something urgent that must be dealt with first, exactly a pressing matter.

clue.text: Kind of red coat worn by clubber, periodically

indicators.note: a coat worn by someone wraps around them, so the coat goes round the kept letters

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of clubber

explanation.surface: Describing a red coat that a nightclub-goer wears now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Malbec is a grape variety and the red wine made from it, notably in Argentina, so it is a kind of red.

clue.text: Boss working hard to clear debts

indicators.note: to clear debts is to wipe them out, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: a studious person works hard at their books
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A manager toiling away to pay off what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss looks like a person in charge, but here it is a raised knob or stud on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round ornamental knob projecting from a surface, which is the same thing as a stud.

clue.text: I must leave Munich's beer supply for admired figure there

indicators.note: read as supple-y, meaning flexibly, so the remaining letters bend into a new order
the letter I has to go, so it is struck from the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A Bavarian beer cellar telling a customer to clear off so a famous drinker can be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a noun for the beer stock, but it is the adverb from supple. 'There' points back to Munich, so the definition wants a German word.
explanation.definitionFit: Übermensch is Nietzsche's German term for a superman, an idealised being looked up to in Germany.

clue.text: Maybe Rooney's drunk, snorting cocaine, right?

indicators.note: snorting takes something in through the nose, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a souse is a habitual drunkard
C is drug slang for cocaine
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip asking whether the footballer was drunk and taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The C goes in after the first letter: S + C + OUSE, then R. Wayne Rooney, the footballer, comes from Liverpool, and a Scouser is someone from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouser is the informal name for a native of Liverpool, and Rooney is one example, hence Maybe.

clue.text: Don't talk about something downloaded by love poet

indicators.note: about means going round, so the hush word surrounds the download

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
an app is a program you download to a phone
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet about a file you got from a romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love poet' looks like one phrase, but love only supplies the final letter; the definition is just poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the ancient Greek lyric poet of Lesbos, famed for her verse.

clue.text: Sing about free ride, with intro from Stevie Nicks

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sing word wraps around the free ride

parts.note: to sing and to shop are both slang for informing on someone

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Stevie
a lift is a free ride in someone's car

explanation.surface: Song lyrics about hitching a lift, with Stevie Nicks of Fleetwood Mac introducing them.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevie Nicks reads as a singer's name, but Nicks is the definition. The first letter of Stevie extends the sing word before it wraps round the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and shoplifts means steals goods from a store.

clue.text: Addicts keeping sober, with flipping rowdy encouragement

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the addicts surround the sober letters

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a body of recovering addicts
TT means teetotal, never drinking

indicators.note: flipping turns something over, so the word for rowdy is read backwards

parts.note: a yob is a rowdy lout

explanation.surface: Recovering addicts staying dry while being cheered by a noisy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild swear word qualifying rowdy, but it signals the reversal of YOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Attaboy is an exclamation of praise urging someone on, so a form of encouragement.

clue.text: Marina may welcome these revolutionary extremists from steadfast, heroic army

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the gathered letters run backwards
extremists are at the far ends, so only the outer letters of each word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of steadfast
first and last letters of heroic
first and last letters of army

explanation.surface: Someone named Marina sheltering a band of rebels from a brave, resolute army.
explanation.walkthrough: Marina reads as a woman's name, but it is a harbour for pleasure boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a dock for small pleasure craft, so it welcomes boats such as these sailing vessels.

clue.text: In blocking Porto's wingers fail to disrupt a shot

indicators.note: blocking means getting in the way, so the first word sits in the middle of the other
wingers play on the flanks, so only the two edge letters of the city are taken

parts.note: the outer letters of Porto
in and hot both mean fashionable
to bomb is to fail badly

explanation.surface: A football report on Porto's wide men failing to get past a defensive block.
explanation.walkthrough: The football words lead you to expect a match; In is a word in its own right meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: To photobomb is to jump into someone else's photograph uninvited, spoiling the picture.

clue.text: Doctor grasps paper by cooler physicist

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tight, so the doctor's letters close round the paper

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
i is the name of a British newspaper, sister to the Independent
AC is air conditioning, a cooler

explanation.surface: A medic clutching a newspaper beside an air-conditioning unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was the British theoretical physicist who shared the 1933 Nobel Prize for quantum mechanics.

clue.text: Prince Albert's accepted in Abu Dhabi, say

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
Al is a short form of Albert

explanation.surface: A royal visitor named Albert being welcomed in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Albert reads as one royal name, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal means permissible under Islamic law, as food is in a Muslim country such as the UAE.

clue.text: Maybe Labour, and its old leader Miliband, like Messi?

parts.note: Labour is an example of a left-wing party
Michael Foot led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
Ed Miliband led Labour from 2010 to 2015

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Labour and its leaders resemble a famous footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Messi is famous for kicking with his left foot, so he is left-footed.

clue.text: Corrupt person's confession probed by new copper in office

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so the confession has the other letters pushed into it

parts.note: a crook admitting it would say I'm bent, bent being slang for corrupt
N is the abbreviation for new
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A crooked official owning up while questioned by a rookie police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal. The new letters go in straight after the confession's opening I.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, incumbent describes someone currently holding a post, so in office.

clue.text: English playmaker has heart, not retreating

parts.note: the heart of something is its middle

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the little word is read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for an English midfielder who has courage and never backs off.
explanation.walkthrough: Playmaker suggests a football midfielder, but it means a writer of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Middleton was an English Jacobean dramatist, author of The Changeling, so literally a maker of plays.

clue.text: Remake of Godfather's iffy? Yes, but it's a spanking tale

indicators.note: a remake makes the thing over again in new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A film critic doubting a remake of The Godfather yet admitting it is a cracking story.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanking sounds like the British sense of excellent, but it is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty Shades of Grey is E. L. James's erotic novel, famous for its scenes of spanking and bondage.

clue.text: Bad reaction to bloomers in comic play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an allergy to pollen from flowering plants

explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers suggests underwear, but here it means plants in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the pollen allergy that makes people sneeze and Coward's farce about the eccentric Bliss family.

clue.text: Lass excited about turning up silk trousers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
about means around, so the jumbled girl goes round the other piece
excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a silk is a senior barrister, a King's Counsel or KC, who wears a silk gown

explanation.surface: A girl thrilled to show off her silk trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Silk looks like the cloth of the trousers, but it is a senior lawyer, who 'takes silk' on promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are loose casual trousers, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Maybe Rachel Riley's beginning to bore devoted fan

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the single letter goes inside the fan

parts.note: a fiend is an enthusiast, as in a fitness fiend

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is its first letter, so only that is used

parts.note: first letter of Riley

explanation.surface: Rachel Riley of Countdown starting to tire an adoring follower.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Riley is the Countdown TV presenter, but the definition is only Maybe Rachel: Rachel Green is a character in the sitcom Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachel is one of the six characters of the sitcom Friends, so she is an example of a friend.

clue.text: Is dishonest politician investing francs in account?

indicators.note: investing means putting money in, so the currency letter goes inside the word for dishonesty

parts.note: someone who is dishonest lies
F is the abbreviation for franc
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Asking whether a crooked MP is putting foreign money into a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: Account suggests a bank, but it means a narrative of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A life story is a narrative of someone's life, and an account is a telling of events.

clue.text: See 16
What American held in hands for composer

indicators.note: something held in a pair of hands is gripped between them, so the letters sit inside

parts.note: left and right hands, L and R
eh? is a way of asking what?
A is a common abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what an American was clutching for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Austro-Hungarian composer of operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Harsh noise from King Charles by his hiding place

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
Charles II hid in an oak tree after the battle of Worcester in 1651

explanation.surface: A rasping sound coming from the king near the spot where he hid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Oak at Boscobel, where the future Charles II hid from Parliament's soldiers, is a famous story in English history.
explanation.definitionFit: A croak is a deep, rough cry such as a frog makes, a harsh noise.

clue.text: Insert tip of needle into clothing — so do this?

definitions.text: Insert tip of needle into clothing — so do this?

indicators.note: Insert tells you to push one piece inside another, here the needle's point going into the outfit
into names the receiving word, the clothing, that takes the extra letter

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit or PE kit

indicators.note: the tip of a needle is its point, so only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: first letter of needle

explanation.surface: An instruction to poke a needle point into a garment, then a wry question about whether that is the craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the definition: pushing needle tips through yarn to make clothes is exactly what this activity is.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting means making garments by looping yarn with needles, so it is what you do by working needle points into clothing.

clue.text: River carp sandwiches put away

indicators.note: a sandwich has its filling between two slices, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to carp and to grouse both mean to complain
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A fish swallowing sandwiches that someone had stored.
explanation.walkthrough: Carp looks like the fish, but it is a verb meaning grumble. GR + EAT + OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Ouse is a long river in eastern England, flowing through Bedford and Ely to the Wash.

clue.text: Ms Quatro has lowered head and arms

indicators.note: in a down clue, lowering the head moves the top letter to the bottom

parts.note: Suzi Quatro is the American rock singer and bassist

explanation.surface: The rock singer bowing and spreading her arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Arms looks like limbs, but here it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Uzis are Israeli submachine guns, and arms means weapons.

clue.text: Mobster, I learn, essentially unable to create issue

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the phrase, where the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A gangster discovering he cannot father children.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue here means children, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for offspring, so someone sterile cannot produce children.

clue.text: Bored taking cannabis, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks about what was spoken, so we go by the sound

parts.note: someone taking cannabis is on weed, weed being slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone asking if a listless friend has been smoking dope.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived word is said roughly as on-wee-d.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennuied means affected by ennui, the French word for listless weariness, so bored.
